questions: Did the stiffness develop gradually over months or years rather than over days or weeks?
Do sudden noises, touch, movement, or emotional stress trigger painful muscle spasms or worsening stiffness?
Do you remain fully conscious during these spasms?
Is the stiffness substantially reduced during sleep?
Have you had episodes of muscle spasms affecting the abdomen, back, legs, or face?
Have you had difficulty moving your eyes up or down, or difficulty keeping your eyes open?
Have you experienced fainting, marked dizziness on standing, urinary retention or incontinence, constipation, or erectile dysfunction?
Have you had a reduced sense of smell, dream-enactment behavior, or a tremor?
Have you had slowness of movement, reduced facial expression, soft speech, or small handwriting?
Have you had frequent falls, especially early in the illness?
Is one side of the body substantially more affected than the other?
Does one limb feel as though it moves on its own or does not belong to you?
Have you had difficulty performing learned purposeful actions despite understanding what you want to do?
Have you had double vision, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or poor coordination?
Have you had numbness, weakness, or exaggerated reflexes in addition to the stiffness?
Have you had seizures, confusion, memory decline, or major changes in behavior?
Did the symptoms begin after starting or increasing an antipsychotic, antiemetic, or other dopamine-blocking medication?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, cancer, or another autoimmune disorder?
Have you had a recent infection, cancer diagnosis, or unexplained weight loss?
Have you been tested for antibodies associated with stiff-person syndrome or autoimmune neurologic disease?

results: 1. Comprehensive movement-disorders and neurologic examination, including vertical and horizontal saccades, smooth pursuit, vestibulo-ocular reflex, eyelid opening, postural stability, gait, cerebellar function, and pyramidal signs
cranial nerve examination: supranuclear vertical gaze palsy with preserved horizontal gaze; severe dysarthria and dysphagia
mental status / cognitive screen: MoCA 24/30; frontal assessment battery 13/18
muscle tone examination: severe axial neck rigidity; mild upper-limb rigidity
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal power
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal limb coordination; impaired truncal stability
posture and pull test: axial instability with early falls; abnormal pull test
vertical saccades and gaze range (up and down): both upgaze and downgaze RESTRICTED, vertical worse than horizontal; horizontal gaze preserved
doll's head (oculocephalic) manoeuvre: the gaze restriction is OVERCOME - this is supranuclear, not a nerve or muscle palsy
smooth pursuit and saccade velocity: normal
eyelid function (apraxia of lid opening, blepharospasm, lid retraction): normal
pull test / retropulsion: not performed
gait observation including turning and doorways: not recorded
limb rigidity and axial (neck) rigidity: SEVERE in the neck, mild in the upper limbs - axial predominance
cerebellar testing (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, tandem gait): normal
2. MRI of the brain with and without contrast, including diffusion-weighted imaging and thin-slice midbrain sequences
MRI brain with gadolinium: mild midbrain atrophy with hummingbird sign; no abnormal enhancement
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: normal
MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio): mild hummingbird sign with cerebral atrophy
